subject: Initial call — logging, PII & retention requirements (Paxion Health)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@paxionhealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Initial call — logging, PII & retention requirements (Paxion Health)

Hi Elena (and Paxion security team),

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap from our discovery call and a proposed set of next steps so we’re aligned. High-level summary:

Pain points discussed:
- Unpredictable costs from broad token logging across LLM calls.
- Concern about accidental persistence of PHI/SSNs in model cache or logs.
- Need for auditable trails for requests and admin actions (regulatory + internal audit).

Current stack you described:
- Front-end app -> API gateway -> internal service -> Redwood-hosted inference (pilot).
- Identity + SSO via Okta, events logged to Splunk for business metrics.

Success criteria you called out:
- No raw PHI in long-term logs (redaction or not stored).
- Ability to provide per-request audit records for at least key events.
- Ability to choose data residency (US-only) and KMS integration for customer keys.

Privacy/logging constraints you emphasized:
- Strict requirement that raw LLM traces containing PHI be redacted or never persisted beyond short retention (you mentioned ~90 days as a target for traces, with audit event retention longer).
- Need for the ability to disable or opt-out of KV cache per workload.
- Requirement to produce human-readable audit logs for compliance requests.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) I’ll send our data-handling one-pager and a short security questionnaire for your security/procurement teams (attached).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Dev (SE) to go through logging controls and KMS options — suggested week of Feb 22.
3) If the security questionnaire looks ok, we’ll provide a SOC2 report link and sample audit log export format.

Action items:
- Elena: confirm whether 90-day max for traces is strict, and whether audit-event retention needs to be 6+ years for regulatory reasons.
- Paxion security: note any additional format requirements for audit exports (CSV vs JSON).

Thanks — I’m looping in Dev to answer technical questions.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0147

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@paxionhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Paxion Security <security@paxionhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@paxionhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 17:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial call — logging, PII & retention requirements (Paxion Health)

Thanks Vanessa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 90-day retention target applies to LLM-level traces (model inputs/outputs) only. Core security/audit events (who requested what, timestamps, admin actions) must be retained for 7 years per our compliance requirements.
- We need out-of-the-box redaction for common PHI patterns (SSNs, MRNs, DOB) and the ability to bring our own regexes for custom identifiers. We’d prefer server-side redaction before anything is written to durable storage.
- KV/cache: we must be able to disable KV cache for specific routes that handle PHI.
- Data residency: all inference and logs containing sensitive data must remain in US regions; cross-border movement requires explicit approval.

Procurement has asked that any evidence (SOC2, penetration test summary) be accessible via link or secure transfer, and that we have an exportable audit log sample in CSV format.

I’ll review the questionnaire once you send it. Two quick asks: can you confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys in KMS (we prefer CMEK), and whether audit logs can be pulled via API on demand?

—Elena
Director, Product Security | Paxion Health
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@paxionhealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 08:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial call — logging, PII & retention requirements (Paxion Health)

Hi Elena — quick technical responses to your questions and options we can present in the SE deep-dive: 

1) Redaction approaches we support:
   - Server-side regex redaction pipeline (configurable, runs before persistent logging).
   - PII-detection model to identify and redact entities even when formats vary.
   - Post-processing hooks so Paxion can inject custom redaction rules.

2) Caching and KV control:
   - Per-route KV cache toggle: can disable on a route-by-route basis.
   - For extra safety we can run those routes on a dedicated pool with no shared KV caching.

3) Audit & export:
   - Audit events (request id, user id, timestamp, model version, route) are exportable via API and available in CSV/JSON.
   - We can provide a 7-year export archive option for event-level logs.

4) KMS / keys:
   - Support for customer-managed keys (CMEK) in supported cloud regions; keys are used for at-rest encryption of persisted artifacts.

I’m attaching a short one-pager that outlines the logging and redaction controls and sample audit export headers. We’ll walk through this and run through live settings in the SE session.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com
